chunks: And Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who ordered a free man to kill another man, and he killed him, he عليه السلام said: “The one who directly carried out the killing shall be executed for him, and the one who ordered his killing shall be imprisoned in prison forever until he dies.”

key_terms.أَمَرَ بِقَتْلِهِ: Ordered that the person be killed.
key_terms.وَلِيَ قَتْلَهُ: The one who directly undertook and carried out the killing.
key_terms.يُقْتَلُ بِهِ: He is executed in retaliation for the murder committed.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone orders another person to commit murder?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling in a case where one man orders a free man to kill another person. The direct killer is subject to qisas, while the one who commanded the killing is punished with permanent imprisonment until death, distinguishing between direct commission and instigation.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5210 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Jafar Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) regarding a man who commanded a free man to kill another man, and he carried out the killing.
Imam (as) said: "The one who directly committed the murder shall be executed, and the one who ordered the killing shall be imprisoned forever until he dies."
